goal: Bound the working-agent iteration with the default wall-clock deadline so an invoker that never returns is cancelled and surfaces a timeout-classified failure under the default config, with no operator override required.

relevant: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/harness.py -- around line 3221 the bare `await invoker(request)` path runs when hang_timeout is None/non-positive; this is the unbounded path to bound
packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/harness.py -- _invoke_with_watchdog around line 2860 is the existing silence watchdog; the wall-clock deadline is additive to it
references: .flywheel/specs/00066-FEATURE-universal-deadlines.md -- criterion #2, D-2 (wall-clock not silence), Open Questions (Phase 1 containment seam for the timeout classification)
constraints: Use the deadline primitive and resolved-config ceiling from the prerequisite tasks; do not invent a bespoke timeout here.
Under default config (no override) the agent iteration must run under a finite ceiling -- do NOT leave the bare unbounded await path reachable by default.
A timeout must surface a distinguishable timeout-classified outcome (route into Phase-1 containment if its seam is present), not a silent return or a generic crash.
Keep the existing silence watchdog behavior working; the new bound runs alongside it.
Add the pytest target so `uv run pytest -k harness_agent_deadline` selects it.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify or weaken assertions in test_harness.py or the silence-watchdog tests.
Do not change the rubric, command-grader, docker, or autopilot paths here.
Do not grade the downstream retry policy -- only that the deadline fires and a timeout outcome is surfaced.
edge_cases: An invoker that never returns under DEFAULT config (no override) is cancelled in bounded wall time -- a test that only passes when an override is set is insufficient.
The resolved default agent-iteration ceiling is non-null.
A normally-completing iteration still completes (no false-positive timeout).
